basis: 15 practice sessions (10 hosted cases, 12 suppliers) and 17 sandbox sessions; see sessions.csv / threads.csv / messages.jsonl

findings.title: "agreed" freezes the price unless we give a lever
findings.finding: 16 practice threads reached agreed. In 15 no later move lowered the price: claims, concessions and pushes all got "Our agreed offer stands". The one exception (P02, first run) dropped 0.7 % (369.12 to 366.41) in exchange for 14-day payment. Price moves while the status is open, as a counter to a sheet below its price.
findings.implication: Do not send a sheet the supplier would accept until the price is where we want it. After agreed, only a lever it values (e.g. faster payment) buys more.

findings.title: Same moves, same result
findings.finding: Supplier numbers are deterministic; only the wording varies. Nine identical D01 runs gave identical prices; replays of P04 and P11 matched round for round; P02 differed only because our first offer differed.
findings.implication: Practice replays measure our change, not noise. A simulator of the supplier rules is feasible.

findings.title: Covering the need beats price
findings.finding: P08 and P18 closed 12-month deals on a 24-month need; uncovered need was about half of C. C_best implies 4.27 vs 5.93 (P08) and 3.10 vs 6.00 (P18) at those terms. In P10 a 24-month contract unlocked the full volume (23,400 instead of 19,890).
findings.implication: Fix contract length and volume to cover need x horizon before negotiating price.

findings.title: An instant agree means we offered too much
findings.finding: P05: Dralveck agreed to our first offer (97 % of its quote) in round 1, twice. In the first P05 run our offer sat above Hrvelec's quote and it agreed at once.
findings.implication: Open well below the supplier's price; an agree on the opening sheet is a signal we left money.

findings.title: Persona signals in the notes predict behaviour
findings.finding: price_frozen (P03, P04): no price move, 'group directives, price reductions frozen until December; we can talk about payment, volume or contract length'. cash_need (Dralveck, Fuchsreiter, Kalwisz): 'I need faster payment since cash is tight'. capacity_full (Hrvelec, Ravensteiner): faster delivery costs an overtime premium. spare_capacity: 'We have free capacity for your parts'.
findings.implication: Read the signals before the first move and pick the lever accordingly.

findings.title: Payment days cost the supplier's own rate
findings.finding: Moving payment from 30 to 90 days: free at P08 and P18 (raw-material distributors), +0.7 % at P03 (about 4 %/yr), +1.0 % at P02 (6 %/yr), +1.2 % at P04 (7 %/yr), +1.4 % at P07 (8.5 %/yr); Hrvelec +1.5 to 2.1 % for 45 to 90 days (12 to 17 %/yr). Our cost of money is 8 %/yr.
findings.implication: Take longer payment where the supplier's rate is below 8 %, offer faster payment where it is far above (cash-short suppliers).

findings.title: 24 months is often free
findings.finding: P03, P04, P07 and P10 accepted 24 months at their price ('valuable planning security'). Raw-material distributors (P08, P18) kept 12 months at a fixed price and offered an index clause on AS-14404 instead.
findings.implication: Ask for the full horizon early; for raw material, consider the index clause to get coverage.

findings.title: Verified data rarely moves price
findings.finding: Of 57 arguments, 44 were verified, 11 duplicate and 2 contradicted, but only P01 moved (EUR 1.20 after late notice plus index: 'we did not know that, a fair point'). Rising indices are read as support for the supplier ('Your figures confirm our case'); scorecards 'hold, but do not change our calculation'.
findings.implication: Use claims sparingly and only those that cut against the supplier's stated drivers; never cite a rising index.

findings.title: No thousands separators in figures
findings.finding: '2,637 ppm' was parsed as 2.637 and came back contradicted ('That costs trust'). Written as 2637 in the replay it was verified.
findings.implication: Format every cited figure without separators.

findings.title: In an RFQ a data ID counts once per case
findings.finding: The same index IDs cited to a second bidder came back duplicate. Only rival quotes and offers may be cited to every bidder.
findings.implication: Spread different arguments across bidders; cite rival offers instead.

findings.title: Nobody sends a cost breakdown
findings.finding: 0 of 12 practice suppliers sent one, including those marked open_book. Delivery schedules (P05, P10) and the 8D report (P11) came on request; a quote PDF comes with every changed offer.
findings.implication: Do not spend a round waiting for a breakdown; model cost from should-cost and cost drivers.

findings.title: Bluff and urgency move nothing on an unchanged sheet
findings.finding: Three runs each on D01: the back office said 'My call: hold' every time and the final price was identical. The words register ('built on mutual reliability, not on pressure').
findings.implication: Pressure without a term-sheet move is wasted; never leak urgency.

findings.title: Every session reveals the floor
findings.finding: C_best comes back with the result even after a walk-away, so one practice session per case gives its best achievable cost.
findings.implication: sessions.csv c_best is the target for every hosted case.
